newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran MPs reject German parliament criticism.
newsitem.headline: Iran MPs reject German parliament criticism.

text.p: A majority of Iranian parliament deputies on Wednesday rejected criticism from their German counterparts after a Berlin court accused Tehran leaders of ordering political killings.
The Iranian news agency IRNA said 160 members of Iran's 270-seat parliament signed a statement rejecting as "hasty" the German parliamentary move last week supporting the court's verdict.

The court two weeks ago jailed an Iranian and three Lebanese for the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin, and said Tehran's leaders had ordered the killings. Iran has repeatedly denied all involvement.
"This move shows that the inability to take wise decisions has deep roots in the ruling institutions of this country (Germany)," said the statement, quoted by the daily Ettelaat.

The MPs called on Iran's government to reciprocate German actions and "set the level of political, economic and cultural ties with Germany in proportion to this country's independence from America and Zionism," the Iranian newpaper said.

Iranian leaders have blamed the United States and Israel -- the Islamic republic's arch enemies -- for being behind the verdict and instigating a row between Tehran and Bonn, until recently Iran's main trade partner.
The statement also urged the government to follow up a lawsuit against German companies accused of helping Baghdad produce chemical weapons in the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
